**Proposed mechanism:** PCBD1 (HGNC:8875) —DISRUPTS→ 4a-hydroxy-tetrahydrobiopterin (CHEBI:17788); 4a-hydroxy-tetrahydrobiopterin (CHEBI:17788) —DECREASES→ Tyrosine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70317); Tyrosine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70317) —LEADS_TO→ Hypopigmentation (HP:0001009); PAH (HGNC:8604) —DISRUPTS→ Phenylalanine (CHEBI:17317); Phenylalanine (CHEBI:17317) —DECREASES→ Phenylalanine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70306); Phenylalanine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70306) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Phenylalanine metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70306) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Mutations in PCBD1 lead to a deficiency in pterin-4 alpha-carbinolamine dehydratase 1, impairing the regeneration of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), a crucial cofactor for aromatic amino acid hydroxylases. This deficiency disrupts tyrosine metabolism and can lead to hypopigmentation. Concurrently, mutations in PAH cause phenylketonuria, leading to the accumulation of phenylalanine, which disrupts phenylalanine metabolism. Both disruptions in aromatic amino acid metabolism converge on shared downstream phenotypic consequences such as intellectual disability and seizures, reflecting a common pathway of neurodevelopmental compromise due to metabolic dysregulation.
